title: The Euro Currency officially became the legal tender for France, along with the other European Union (EU) Eurozone member area countries, replacing the French franc by being introduced physically with the official launch of the currency…
text: The euro is the official currency of 21 of the 27 member states of the European Union. This group of states is officially known as the euro area, more commonly named the eurozone.

title: France agrees to return the remains of Saartjie Baartman to South Africa.
text: Sarah Baartman, also spelled Sara, sometimes in the Dutch diminutive form Saartje (Afrikaans: ), or Saartjie, and Bartman, Bartmann, was a Khoekhoe woman who was exhibited as a freak show attraction in 19th-century Europe under the name Hottentot Venus, a name that was later attributed to at least one other woman similarly exhibited.

title: first round of the presidential election: Jacques Chirac and Jean-Marie le Pen poll the most votes. This was a major political event, both nationally and internationally, as it was the first time someone Le Pen with such far-right views…
text: Presidential elections were held in France on 21 April 2002, with a runoff election between the top two candidates, incumbent Jacques Chirac of the Rally for the Republic and Jean-Marie Le Pen of the National Front, on 5 May. This presidential contest attracted a greater than usual amount of international attention because of candidate Le Pen's unexpected appearance in the runoff election.

title: second round of the presidential election. Jacques Chirac returns for a second term as President of the French Republic.
text: Jacques René Chirac was President of France from 1995 to 2007. He was previously Prime Minister of France from 1974 to 1976 and 1986 to 1988, as well as Mayor of Paris from 1977 to 1995.

title: nomination of Jean-Pierre Raffarin for the post of Prime Minister.
text: Jean-Pierre Raffarin is a French politician who served as Prime Minister of France from 6 May 2002 to 31 May 2005 under President Jacques Chirac. He resigned after France's rejection of the referendum on the European Union draft constitution.

title: first round of the legislative elections
text: Legislative elections were held in France on 9 and 16 June 2002, to elect the 12th National Assembly of the Fifth Republic, in a context of political crisis. The Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin announced his political retirement after his elimination at the first round of the 2002 presidential elections.

title: Citroën launches a revised model of its popular Berlingo leisure activity vehicle.
text: The Citroën Berlingo and Peugeot Partner are a range of minivans produced since 1996 and marketed under the Citroën and Peugeot marque. They are sold as light commercial vehicles or as a passenger multi-purpose-vehicle variant with rear seats and windows.

title: Renault launches the second generation of Mégane hatchback range of hatchbacks, estates, convertibles and saloons.
text: The Renault Mégane is a small family car produced by the French car manufacturer Renault since 1995, and was the successor to the Renault 19. The Mégane has been offered in three- and five-door hatchback, saloon, coupé, convertible and estate bodystyles at various points in its lifetime, and having been through four generations is now in its fifth incarnation.

title: The Renault Megane II is voted European Car of the Year.
text: The European Car of the Year award is an international Car of the Year award established in 1964 by a collective of automobile magazines from different countries in Europe. The current organising media of the award are Auto, Autocar (United Kingdom), Autopista (Spain), Autovisie (Netherlands), L'Automobile Magazine (France), Stern (Germany) and Vi Bilägare (Sweden).

title: Danyel Waro, fyer bâtard documentary film is released.
text: Danyel Waro, fyer bâtard is a 2002 documentary film.

title: Trident Media Guard company is founded.
text: Trident Media Guard is a French company that specializes in software to prevent unauthorized copying of files over the Internet. Founded in 2002 by Alain Guislain and Bastien Casalta, it is located in Saint-Sébastien-sur-Loire near Nantes.

title: Tour de France begins.
text: The 2002 Tour de France was a multiple-stage bicycle race held from 6 to 28 July, and the 89th edition of the Tour de France. The event started in Luxembourg and ended in Paris.

title: French Grand Prix won by Michael Schumacher of Germany.
text: Michael Schumacher is a German former racing driver who competed in Formula One from 1991 to 2006 and from 2010 to 2012. Schumacher won a record-setting seven Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles, tied by Lewis Hamilton in 2020, and—at the time of his retirement—held the records for most wins (91), pole positions (68), and podium finishes (155), while he maintains the record for most fastest laps (77), a…

title: Tour de France ends, won by Lance Armstrong of the United States.
text: Lance Edward Armstrong is an American former professional road racing cyclist. He achieved international fame for winning the Tour de France a record seven consecutive times from 1999 to 2005, but was stripped of his titles in 2012 after an investigation into doping allegations found that Armstrong used performance-enhancing drugs over his career.

title: Janvier : Yves Saint Laurent annonce prendre sa retraite et cesser ses activités de haute couture. Dernier défilé également de Courrèges.
text: La haute couture est le secteur professionnel dans lequel exercent les créateurs de vêtements de luxe. Aujourd'hui, elle s'organise autour de « maisons de haute couture », des enseignes pour certaines assez anciennes, auxquelles de nombreux grands couturiers ont collaboré au fil des années.

title: Astérix et Obélix : Mission Cléopâtre, réalisé par Alain Chabat qui joue également le personnage de Jules César et mettant en vedette Christian Clavier (Astérix), Gérard Depardieu (Obélix), Jamel Debbouze (Numérobis), Claude Rich…
text: Alain Chabat est un acteur, réalisateur, scénariste, producteur, humoriste et animateur de télévision français, né le 24 novembre 1958 à Oran. Révélé sur Canal+ en tant que membre du groupe comique Les Nuls, il devient ensuite une des figures de la comédie dans le cinéma français.

title: Monsieur Batignole
text: Le 6 mars est le 65e jour, moins souvent le 66e, de l'année du calendrier grégorien ; il en reste ensuite 300. C'était généralement le 16e jour du mois de ventôse dans le calendrier républicain / révolutionnaire français officiellement dénommé jour de l'épinard.

title: Tableau de famille (Le fate ignoranti), film italien de Ferzan Özpetek
text: Le cinéma italien, qui est le cinéma produit ou réalisé en Italie, est l'un des principaux cinémas nationaux de l'histoire du cinéma. L’histoire du cinéma italien a commencé quelques mois après que les frères Lumière eurent présenté au public leur appareil original, le Cinématographe, le 28 décembre 1895 à Paris : ce sont eux qui l'introduisent en Italie au cours de l'année 1896.

title: César du meilleur film : Le Fabuleux Destin d'Amélie Poulain, de Jean-Pierre Jeunet
text: Le César du meilleur film est une récompense cinématographique française décernée par l'Académie des arts et techniques du cinéma depuis la première remise de prix le 3 avril 1976 au Palais des congrès à Paris.

title: Prix Jean-Vigo : Royal Bonbon, de Charles Najman
text: Le prix Jean-Vigo est une récompense cinématographique française décernée depuis 1951.

title: “La musique” by Star Academy
text: "La Musique" is a 2001 song recorded by the contestants of the first edition of French TV reality show Star Academy. The song was released as a single in December 2001 from the album L'Album and also recorded in a live version on the album Live.

title: “J'ai tout oublié” by Marc Lavoine and Cristina Marocco
text: "J'ai tout oublié" is a 2001 song recorded as a duet by the French artist Marc Lavoine and the Italian singer Cristina Marocco. The song was released on 19 November 2001 as the second single from Lavoine's eighth album, just entitled Marc Lavoine.
listen: J'ai tout oublié Marc Lavoine and Cristina Marocco

title: “Qui est l'exemple?” by Rohff
text: "Qui est l'exemple?" is a 2001 song recorded by French artists Rohff & Kayliah. It was the third single from his debut album, La Vie avant la mort, and was released in late 2001 in a CD maxi, then in February 2002 in a CD single.

title: “Whenever, Wherever” by Shakira
text: "Whenever, Wherever" is a song recorded by Colombian singer-songwriter Shakira for her debut English-language studio album, Laundry Service, her fifth overall. Shakira produced the track and wrote the lyrics to the original Spanish version, titled "Suerte" (English: "Good luck"), which Gloria Estefan later adapted to English.

title: “Tous ensemble” by Johnny Hallyday
text: "Tous Ensemble" is a song recorded in 2002 by French singer Johnny Hallyday. The song was released as a single on 23 April 2002.

title: “Stach Stach” by Bratisla Boys
text: "Stach Stach" is a 2002 song recorded by Michael Youn and his band Bratisla Boys. This humoristic song was released as first single from the album Anthologigi, in April 2002.

title: “Un enfant de toi” by Marlène Duval and Phil Barney
text: "Un Enfant de toi" is a 1987 pop song recorded by the French singer Phil Barney. It was released as a single twice : first in 1987 from the album Recto-verseau, then as a duet with Marlène Duval in 2002.
listen: Un enfant de toi Marlène Duval and Phil Barney

title: “Cum-cum mania” by Félicien
text: "Cum-cum mania" is the name of a 2002 song recorded by Félicien, a contestant of the French reality show Loft Story, broadcast during the spring of that year. Released as his debut single in June 2002, it surprisingly became a huge hit in France and Belgium.

title: “J'ai demandé à la lune” by Indochine
text: "J'ai demandé à la lune" is a song by the French new wave band Indochine, from their 2002 album Paradize. Written by Mickaël Furnon, the singer of Mickey 3D, the song was released as the second single from the album in March 2002 and quickly became a national success, topping the French Singles Chart and selling over 750,000 units in France alone.
listen: J'ai demandé à la lune Indochine

title: “Inch'Allah” by MC Solaar
text: Claude Honoré M'Barali, professionally known as MC Solaar (pronounced ), is a French rapper of Senegalese and Chadian origin. He is one of France's most famous and influential hip-hop artists.

title: “Asereje” by Las Ketchup
text: "The Ketchup Song" (Andalusian pronunciation: ) is a song by Spanish pop group Las Ketchup, released as the lead single from their debut studio album, Hijas del Tomate (2002). The song is about a young man who enters a nightclub while singing and dancing.

title: “Marie” by Johnny Hallyday
text: "Marie" is a 2002 song recorded by French singer Johnny Hallyday. It was the first single from his album À la vie, à la mort !, and was released in October 2002.

title: “Plus haut” by Whatfor
text: Whatfor is the name of the band created by the second season of the popular French reality-TV show Popstars aired on RTL Group TV channel M6 in fall 2002. The group consisted of Cyril and Erika, Nicolas (from Toulon) and Monia (from the Lyon suburbs).

title: “Paris Latino” by Star Academy 2
text: "Paris Latino" is the debut single by French band Bandolero, released in 1983. In 2002, the song was successfully covered by Star Academy 2.

title: “Tu trouveras” by Natasha St-Pier
text: "Tu trouveras" is the name of a 2002 song recorded by Canadian singer Natasha St-Pier and French singer Pascal Obispo. It was composed by Obispo and written by Lionel Florence.

title: “Ti amo (rien que des mots)” by Umberto Tozzi & Lena Ka
text: Umberto Antonio Tozzi is an Italian pop and rock singer and songwriter. Throughout his career, he has sold over 70 million records in different languages internationally.
listen: Ti amo (rien que des mots) Umberto Tozzi & Lena Ka

title: “Manhattan-Kaboul” by Renaud & Axelle Red
text: "Manhattan-Kaboul" is a French song written by Renaud and composed by Jean-Pierre Bucolo, sung by Renaud in duo with Axelle Red, from the album Boucan d'enfer. It was written in the aftermath of the incidents of September 11, 2001 and the War in Afghanistan.

title: “Musique” by Star Academy 2
text: Star Academy is a French reality singing competition produced by Endemol France. Forming part of the Star Academy franchise, it has been broadcast on TF1 and NRJ 12 (2012–2013).
